title: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL
description: Compare the three most common API protocols for microservices communication.

data.text: Choosing the right communication protocol is critical for microservices performance and developer experience. Netflix, Google, and GitHub each chose different protocols based on their specific needs. Understanding the trade-offs helps you make the right choice.

REST (Representational State Transfer) uses standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and is the most widely adopted protocol. It is simple, human-readable, and works well with web technologies. However, it can be verbose and lacks strong typing.

gRPC, developed by Google, uses Protocol Buffers for binary serialization and HTTP/2 for transport. It is extremely fast, strongly typed, and supports bi-directional streaming. However, it requires code generation and is less human-readable than REST.

GraphQL, developed by Facebook, lets clients request exactly the data they need via a single endpoint. It reduces over-fetching and under-fetching but introduces query complexity and caching challenges.

cards.title: GraphQL
cards.description: Query language, single endpoint, flexible queries

data.title: Protocol Selection Tip
data.text: Use REST for public APIs and simple services. Use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication where performance matters. Use GraphQL when clients need flexible data fetching, such as mobile or web frontends.

items.question: Can I mix protocols in one system?
items.answer: Yes. Many companies use REST for public APIs, gRPC for internal services, and GraphQL for frontend data fetching. An API gateway can translate between them.

items.question: Which is fastest?
items.answer: gRPC is generally the fastest due to binary serialization and HTTP/2. REST is slower but often fast enough. GraphQL performance depends on query complexity.

items.question: What about HTTP/3?
items.answer: HTTP/3 (QUIC) is gaining adoption and will improve REST and gRPC performance, especially for mobile and high-latency networks.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: REST is great for public APIs and simple services
gRPC offers the best performance for internal communication
GraphQL shines when clients need flexible data fetching
Mixing protocols is common and often beneficial
data.takeaway: Choose the protocol that matches your use case; do not default to one protocol for everything.
